display.title: Chai V'Kayam: The Rabbi Who Trusted Only Hashem
display.summary_short: For Elul: real teshuvah means trusting that Hashem has erased the past, and a poor rabbi realizes that only Hashem is surely alive, rich and kind.
display.summary_long: In the month of Elul, as Rosh Hashanah approaches, the storyteller explains that teshuvah means returning to our true self, like washing a diamond that never lost its value. The yetzer hara tries to convince us that our teshuvah was not good enough, but when Hashem says a sin is erased, we must trust Him. The Rebbe told a worried young woman to count how many Yom Kippurs had passed, and a car has a huge windshield and only a small mirror for looking back. Then a bitachon story from the time of the Chozeh of Lublin: a poor town rabbi's wife urges him to ask his millionaire brother in Moscow for money to marry off their daughters. He sets out, but returns within moments with three questions: is his brother still alive, still rich, and still generous? Only Hashem is surely all three, so they will trust Him. Two days later a poritz leaves a sack of gold with the rabbi, saying it is his if he does not return in three days. Months later the rabbi asks the Chozeh whether to use it, and the Chozeh greets him with his own words: Hashem lives forever, is always rich and loves to give.
display.lesson: Trust that Hashem forgives completely when we do teshuvah, and rely on Hashem, Who is always alive, always rich and always kind.
